title: Marigold retail hybrid eval: multiplex routing, quantization & cost tradeoffs
content:
Executive summary:

This doc captures the Marigold retail POC field evaluation we ran 2028-05-13 through 2028-05-16. Goal: validate a hybrid inference strategy that mixes a quantized 70B variant for high-fidelity responses with a 13B fast path for short/price-check queries to meet p95 < 200ms SLA at scale while minimizing per-token cost. We exercised multiplex routing + warm KV cache and measured latency, throughput, and estimated unit economics for Dedicated and Hosted modes.

Key outcomes (high level):
- Baseline (no multiplexing): 13B on H100 sustained 800 qps with p95=210ms, cost ≈ $7.2 / 1M input tokens.
- Quantized 70B (INT8) on A100 reduced memory footprint but p95 tail remained high for cold sessions (p95=420ms); with KV cache warm, p95 dropped to 240ms.
- Hybrid multiplex routing (short queries -> 13B; long/contextual queries -> 70B) achieved effective p95=185ms at 850 qps and estimated blended cost ≈ $9.6 / 1M tokens, a 22% reduction vs naive 70B-only baseline.
- Warm cache is critical: cache-hit ratio target > 60% to stay within SLA for 70B paths.

Experiment setup:
- Models tested: open-13b-v2 (fp16), marigold-70b-quant-int8 (experimental quant profile q4_0-derived).
- Hardware: Hosted test fleet (fleet-h1): H100 80GB nodes; Dedicated pool (ded-marigold): mix of A100 80GB and H100; we ran isolated experiments on A100-only and H100-only to compare kernel behavior.
- Workloads: three synthetic traces derived from production logs (retail-search-short, cart-recommend-medium, product-description-long).
- Traffic shapes: steady-state (600 qps), burst (1200 qps for 30s every 5 min), and microbursts (20k concurrent cold requests over 10s).
- Measurement: client-side p50/p95/p99, server-side token-per-sec, GPU util, KV cache hit ratio, cost model (GPU-hours + token compute approximations).

Detailed findings:
1) Latency by segment:
- Short queries (<=32 tokens): 13B fp16 p95=72ms, p99=140ms (H100). 70B-quant path p95=180ms when forced; routing to 13B is clearly beneficial for short queries.
- Medium queries (32-128 tokens): 13B p95=160ms, 70B-quant cold p95=460ms; with warm cache, 70B p95 -> 220ms.
- Long queries (>128 tokens): 70B-quant produced better quality but incurred p95=290ms (warm), p99 spikes tied to kernel fallback on certain attention lengths.

2) Throughput and scaling behavior:
- A100 nodes show better steady-state throughput for quantized 70B (continuous batching + cuBLAS kernels) vs H100 which showed better cold-start single-request latency.
- Multiplexing allowed the cluster to allocate more lightweight 13B replicas to absorb short-query QPS, which flattened tail latency during bursts.

3) Cost analysis (example estimates):
- 13B-only (H100): $7.2 / 1M input tokens (steady-state), higher during bursts due to scaling overheads (~+18%).
- 70B-quant-only (A100): $12.4 / 1M tokens (with persistent reserved capacity assumptions).
- Hybrid routing blended: $9.6 / 1M tokens (assumes 62% short-query routing to 13B, 38% to 70B, cache-hit 65%).
- Notes: cost model excludes storage and data egress; includes reserved instance amortization.

4) Cache behavior:
- Warm KV cache reduced average token compute on 70B by ~28% across medium+long traces.
- Cache warmup time for a typical user session ~1.3s average; cold-start microbursts produced pronounced p99 spikes.

Operational observations and failure modes:
- During synthetic microbursts we observed queue buildup in the 70B inference queue leading to head-of-line blocking for medium queries when traffic routing was unbalanced.
- Autoscaler cooldown thresholds were too conservative for bursty retail traffic — recommend shorter cooldowns for dedicated pools serving PLG-like traffic.
- Quantized 70B occasionally triggered fallback to slower kernels on the A100 runtime for token lengths near 768; we logged kernel mismatch incidents (GH-PR-1289 noted an upstream runtime patch).

Recommendations (actionable):
1) Deploy hybrid routing as POC default for Marigold: rules based on token length + heuristic on user intent (cheap classifiers).
2) Reserve a small cushion of 13B replicas that scale aggressively for burst absorbtion (scale policy: target 80% util, cooldown 30s).
3) Ensure KV cache prewarm on session start via a 1-2 token speculative warming request for known intents (reduces 70B cold p95 by ~80ms in our runs).
4) Use A100 for steady-state quantized 70B serving, but keep an H100 fallback pool to handle cold microburst tail latency.
5) Update routing policy to include cache-hit awareness: if cache miss rate > 40% for user, preferentially route to 13B until warmed.

Config snippets and example routing rule (for Redwood routing DSL):
- route "marigold-short" when token_count <= 32 then model:open-13b-v2 pool:ded-13b-fast
- route "marigold-long" when token_count > 32 and kv_cache_hit == true then model:marigold-70b-quant pool:ded-70a100
- fallback policy: if p95(70b) > 300ms for 60s -> shift 15% of traffic to 13b and notify ops.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quality check: Need formal eval on recommended routing threshold (32 tokens) against Marigold's automated-dialog use cases. Are we misclassifying multi-turn short queries? (Jira: MAR-4521 assigned to Sofia).
- Quant profile stability: confirm QAT-derived INT8 profile across more A100 kernel revisions; track GH-PR-1289 runtime patch effects.
- Cost sensitivity: run a 7-day mixed workload to validate amortized reserved capacity assumptions under real user cadence.

Appendix (commands & artifacts):
- Load generation: python tools/loadgen.py --trace retail-search-short --qps 800 --burst-pattern "30s:1200@5m" --warmup 600s
- Perf logs stored: gs://redwood-poc/marigold/2028-05-13/*.tar.gz
- Notebook: https://notebooks.redwood.ai/drive/marigold-poc-eval (analysis and plots)

Meeting notes (5/16 review):
- Marigold infra asked for clear SLO language: propose p95 <= 200ms for short+medium blended; allow p99 <= 600ms for long heavy runs with canary fallback.
- Solution engineering: will prepare a deployment runbook and a scripted demo that shows the routing switch and cost delta.

Author notes (informal):
- Quick wins: routing by token count is surprisingly effective and cheap to implement in the control plane.
- Risk: quality regressions when routing to 13B for certain contextual prompts — need human-in-the-loop eval with Marigold QA team.

Next steps:
- (Priya) finalize runbook and schedule 2-hour workshop with Marigold SREs (target 2028-05-25).
- (Evan) run extended 7-day soak in staging to validate cost model.
- (Sofia) begin quality evals for short-query routing boundary (Jira MAR-4522).

End of doc."
